n: Model Tweak Studio: per-model patch profiles
w: Apply small, reversible tweaks to a model without re-downloading it: enable quantized KV cache for a model whose defaults lack it, override context length or RoPE settings the authors specify, fix chat templates, set stop tokens and sampler defaults. Patches are stored as named, shareable profiles keyed by model hash, never by editing the original file.

n: GGUF metadata editor with safe write-copy
w: View and edit GGUF key-value metadata in a validated editor; changes write to a copy with a diff and one-click revert.
A local, updatable database of known per-model fixes (template bugs, stop tokens, KV quirks, recommended samplers) applied automatically, each visible and switchable.

The app installs, verifies (SHA-256) and updates its own inference runtimes (llama.cpp builds per GPU, stable-diffusion.cpp, whisper.cpp, TTS engines) inside its own folder, with version pinning and one-click rollback, so nothing external is ever needed.
Run Cerebro, its runtimes, settings and models entirely from one folder or USB drive with no installation and nothing written elsewhere.
A single offline bundle (app + runtimes + chosen models) that installs on a machine that has never been online, with signature verification.
Export any set of models with their tuned configs and patch profiles to a file or drive and import it on another machine, verified by hash.

Shows what every model costs on disk, finds duplicates across LM Studio, Ollama and other folders, suggests cleanups, and can deduplicate identical files with hard links (never deleting without explicit confirmation).

n: Import existing libraries from LM Studio, Ollama, Jan and GPT4All
w: Detects other apps' model folders and adds their models to Cerebro in place, without copying.
Newest block-diffusion drafter from upstream llama.cpp as a speculation candidate the tuner can measure.
Lightweight drafting heads offered to the speculation tuner where a model has them.

n: Speculative checkpointing for hybrid and recurrent models
w: Uses upstream checkpointing so speculation works on hybrid (linear-attention) models without corrupting recurrent state.
Switch KV cache precision on a loaded model without reloading, using the new upstream endpoint, to free VRAM when a long chat grows.
Research-grade 3-bit KV cache offered behind the quality gate for users who need maximum context, with KL-divergence checks.
Research-stage tree drafting, labelled Experimental and measured before use.
Ask questions about a video file with video-capable multimodal models through llama.cpp's multimodal pipeline, with frame sampling controls.

n: Image tool results in agent loops
w: Tools can return images (screenshots, charts, generated images) that vision models see in the next step.
Import and run ComfyUI workflow files headlessly through a local ComfyUI or Cerebro's own image engine, with the workflow's inputs exposed as a clean form.
Apply style LoRAs and ControlNet guidance (pose, depth, edges) in Image Studio.

n: Image upscaling, background removal and face restore
w: One-click post-processing tools in the gallery using local models.

n: Batch image queue with prompt matrix
w: Queue many generations, vary prompts or seeds across a grid, and compare results side by side.

n: Prompt and settings embedded in generated images
w: Every generated PNG carries its prompt, model and settings so it can be reproduced or remixed later; stripping is one click.
Short text-to-video and image-to-video with local video models (for example Wan) on GPUs that can run them; hardware-gated with the reason shown.
Clone a voice from a short sample with modern local TTS, requiring the user to confirm they have the speaker's consent.

n: Qwen3-TTS, Chatterbox, Kyutai and Supertonic voices
w: Newest local text-to-speech engines offered in the voice picker alongside Kokoro and Piper, each with a preview button.

n: Streaming speech-to-text with Kyutai and Parakeet
w: Low-latency live transcription engines for voice mode and captions.
System-wide live captions of any audio playing on the machine, fully local.
Turn a script or document into narrated audio with multiple voices.
Install MCP servers packaged as .mcpb bundles with one click, verified before install.
Browse and install servers from the official MCP Registry inside the Plugins screen when online; cached listing offline.
Render interactive UI components that MCP servers provide, inside a sandboxed frame.
Opt-in connections to remote MCP servers with the spec's modern authorization flow; local servers need none.
Verify tool definitions against publisher signatures and a policy engine before a plugin's tools are exposed.

n: Import MCP configs from Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code and LM Studio
w: Bring existing MCP server setups over in one click.
Expose Cerebro's local models, document search and image generation to other MCP hosts on the same machine.
Create a simple MCP server from a script or an API description without writing boilerplate, sandboxed by default.
A readable rule file (allow, ask, deny with patterns and conditions, last-match-wins) that power users can edit directly, with a live tester.
Switch between named permission profiles (Cautious, Balanced, Hands-off, custom) per workspace.
Mark folders as trusted for tools; open untrusted projects in a safe mode where hooks, plugins and auto-approvals are disabled.
The coding agent runs git with repository config hooks such as core.fsmonitor neutralised, so opening a hostile repository cannot execute code.
Plugins pinned by commit or hash are verified after checkout, so a pinned reference cannot be redirected.
Chat templates render in a restricted engine that cannot reach the filesystem, network or Python objects.
Model and plugin downloads refuse redirects to local, private or link-local addresses.
Scans documents, plugin descriptions and tool outputs for delayed trigger-style injections and labels them.

n: Per-user isolation of cached tool results
w: Cached tool and MCP results are keyed per user so one user can never receive another's cached result.

n: Continuous CVE feed for bundled runtimes
w: Checks bundled runtime versions against a signed advisory list (offline-cached) and prompts to update affected components.

n: No Python in the shipped app
w: Everything shipped is Rust, native runtimes and the web front end, removing the PyPI supply-chain attack class; optional Python tools are user-installed extras.
Images, audio and large results stream to the UI through a custom protocol instead of IPC, keeping the interface fast.
The app uses its own named WebView2 profile so browser data and extensions never mix with it.
A system-wide shortcut opens a small floating prompt over any app, answers from the local model, and pastes back.
Select text in any app, press a shortcut, choose rewrite, summarize, translate or fix grammar; runs locally.
Capture a region of the screen and ask a vision model about it.
Right-click files or folders to summarize, index, transcribe, translate or ask about them.
Keep models warm in the background with a tray menu for quick actions and status.
A node-graph canvas (like ComfyUI, for language and multimodal pipelines) to chain models, tools, documents and image generation into reusable workflows, runnable on a schedule or from a hotkey.
Save prompts with fill-in variables, organize them in folders, and trigger them from the command palette.
Group chats, documents, memory, models and permissions per project or client.
A notes area and freeform canvas where chat outputs, images and documents can be arranged and edited with AI assistance.
Send one prompt to several models at once and compare answers, speed and cost side by side.
The model writes and runs code (Python via a user-installed runtime, or a bundled WASI runtime) in a sandbox to analyse files, make charts and compute answers.
Open a CSV or Excel file and ask questions, clean data or build charts, computed exactly rather than guessed.
Dedicated translation view for text and documents with glossary support, fully local.
Point at a folder and get an organized summary with citations to each file.
Import an mbox or PST export and search, summarize and draft replies offline.
Shareable, parameterised task recipes (for example 'add tests for this module') that the agent runs step by step.
Pool machines on the home or office network to run models too large for one (llama.cpp RPC), off by default, paired with a one-time code, encrypted and loopback-restricted unless enabled.

n: LAN web access for phones and tablets
w: Opt-in, authenticated, TLS-protected web interface so other devices on the local network can chat with Cerebro.
Export tuned results with full provenance as a file others can import to see how a model runs on similar hardware, with no identifying data.
Import shared result files to see how models perform on hardware like yours before downloading them.
Unfinished chats, queues and downloads resume exactly where they were after a crash or reboot.
One-click support bundle with logs and system info, secrets and prompts removed, that the user can inspect before sharing.
Stable and beta channels, signed updates, and one-click rollback to the previous version.
Pick from curated themes or write custom CSS for the app, safely scoped.
Accessibility presets for contrast, font and spacing.
The interface and help translated into at least twenty languages, with right-to-left support.
Short interactive tours the first time a user opens each major screen, skippable and replayable.
Gentle milestones that introduce advanced features as users grow, never gamified pressure.
Suggests models that fit the user's hardware and how they actually use Cerebro (coding, images, documents), explained.
The user decides which model handles which kind of task (code, quick questions, images) and Cerebro routes automatically.
Preload the models you use at the times you use them so the first answer is instant.
A visible queue of background jobs (tuning, indexing, image batches) with pause, reorder and priority.
An in-app playground and code snippets for calling Cerebro's local API from any language.
Run workflows when a file appears, on a schedule, or from a local script call, never from the internet unless enabled.
Turn rated conversations into a training set and run a local LoRA fine-tune where the hardware allows, gated by a regression check.
Estimates what more VRAM, RAM or a different GPU would unlock for the models the user wants, from measured data.
A tuned profile that minimises watts per token on battery, measured, with the speed trade-off shown.

n: Unified search across chats, documents, images and settings
w: One search box finds anything the user has ever made or configured.
